sentences.text:
Makkhan Kushwaha vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 24
February, 2020
Author: Jagdish Prasad Gupta

Bench: Jagdish Prasad Gupta
 1
 Cr.Rev.No.629/2020
 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 Cr.Rev.No.629/2020
Jabalpur : 24/02/2020
 Shri D.K.Trivedi, Advocate for the applicant.
 Shri Abhinav Dubey, G.A. for the respondent / State.
 Record of both the courts below have been received.
Heard on admission.
Admit.
Also heard on I.A.No.2238/2020, which is an application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

However, at the outset learned counsel for the applicant prays for withdrawal of I.A.No.2238/2020 and prays that this revision may kindly be heard finally as the applicant has completed 25 days in jail custody and he does not want to press this revision on merits and only wants to argue on the point of sentence.
Hence, with the consent of parties, the matter is heard finally.

This revision petition has been filed by the applicant under Section 397/401 of the Cr.P.C. being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 30.1.2020 passed by 28th Addl.
Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District Jabalpur, in Criminal Appeal No.188/2018 partly allowing the appeal and acquitting the applicant for the offence under section 7(i) read with section 16(1)ka(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and affirming the conviction under section 50(1) read with section 7(3) read with section 16(1)ka(ii)
of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 imposed by the trial court and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for 3 months along with fine of Rs.500/-.

sentences.text: Facts, as emerged from the findings of both the courts below and giving rise to the present revision, briefly stated, are that on 13.5.2009 at about 8 AM near Adhartal Police Station, Jabalpur, the applicant accused was found carrying milk in an auto and on being stopped and on enquiry by the local Health officer, he was found selling milk without licence of food item milk under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
The sample was collected by the Health Officer, which was found adulterated.
The offence was registered against the applicant and complaint case was filed before the trial court.
The trial court framed charges against the applicant and after trial convicted and sentenced him as mentioned in the impugned order.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved therewith, this revision has been filed.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the findings of both the courts below are contrary to law.
Statements of the witnesses are not reliable.
The applicant is a first offender and under the aforesaid provision, there is no minimum sentence.
The applicant is facing trial since 2009 and he is in custody since 30.1.2020.
Accordingly, he has completed 25 days imprisonment.
The applicant is not a habitual criminal.

If he is kept in custody for a long time he will come in the contact of hardcore criminals and there will be no possibility of the applicant to reform himself and no purpose will be served as he got sufficient lesson.
In such circumstances, the ends of justice would be met if the applicant is sentenced to the period already undergone by him.
Learned Govt. Advocate appearing for the State has contended that the finding of conviction is based on legal evidence.

So far as the sentence part is concerned, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case exercising discretionary powers the Court may pass appropriate orders and the sentence may be reduced proportionately.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties at length and gone through the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court and also on perusal of the record and statements of witnesses, it is found that the applicant was carrying the milk for selling without licence.

In the circumstances, in view of this Court, the finding of the appellate court with regard to conviction of the applicant for the offence under the aforesaid section does not require any interference as the same is based on sufficient and reliable evidence on record and further appreciation of evidence is not desirable unless the finding is said to be perverse.
Therefore, the same is hereby affirmed.

So far as the prayer with regard to modification of the sentence is concerned, in view of this court,
the applicant is a first offender and is in custody since 30.1.2020, therefore, looking to all circumstances of the case, no useful purpose would be served by keeping the applicant in jail any further.
In these circumstances, the sentence is modified and the applicant is sentenced to the sentence already undergone by him.
The sentence of fine as imposed by the appellate court is affirmed.
Consequently, the criminal revision is partly allowed.
On deposit of the fine amount before the trial Court, the applicant be released forthwith, if not required in any other offence.
Record of the trial Court be sent back immediately to the concerned court below along with a copy of this order for its compliance and necessary action.
C.C. as per rules.
